chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from some of his companions from Aban from Muhammad al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"It is not permissible for a man to sell using a sa' other than the sa' of Egypt, for indeed a man hires a porter and measures for him with the mud of his house, perhaps it is smaller than the mud of the market. And if he said, 'This is smaller than the mud of the market,' he would not take it from him, but he would carry that for him and place it in his trust.' And he said, 'It is not valid except with one mud, and the two amans are at this level (measure).'

key_terms.صَاع: Sa: a traditional unit of volume for dry goods
key_terms.صَاعِ الْمِصْرِ: Sa of Egypt: the standard reference measure
key_terms.مُدّ: Mud: a smaller unit of volume, half a sa'

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using local household measures for trade instead of the standard measure?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on standardizing commercial weights and measures to prevent hidden deception (*gharar*), specifically mandating the use of the recognized 'Sa' of Egypt as the benchmark. It illustrates the practical application of *amanah* (trustworthiness) in trade, where the seller bears the burden of proof and potential liability if a buyer accepts a non-standard, smaller measure, thereby ensuring transparency in market transactions.
